top_story: The killing of two US service members in Jordan on 18 July pushed Washington from a sustained pressure campaign into explicit retaliation, with strikes on Iran entering an eighth consecutive night by 19 July and focusing on targets in Hormozgan as Tehran answered with missiles and drones against Gulf bases. This latest cycle built on several days of escalation in and around the Strait of Hormuz, where US attacks sought to degrade Iranian military capacity and Iranian reprisals widened the battlefield beyond direct US-Iran exchanges. Sirens in Bahrain and Kuwaiti accusations that Tehran targeted civilian infrastructure show how Gulf societies are being drawn into the conflict through fear, disruption, and mounting vulnerability around critical facilities. The immediate trajectory is toward a broader regional war in which retaliatory logic is outpacing diplomacy and exposing both military personnel and civilians to expanding risk.
